reference.name: Panaji (Panjim)
reference.note: 'Panjim, the present capital' = Panaji, capital of Goa; Altinho and Dona Paula are its neighbourhoods.

also known as Panjim, is the capital of the Indian state of Goa

sources.quote: is an old Latin quarter in Panjim, capital city of the state of Goa, India. It maintains its Portuguese influence
narrow and picturesque winding streets like those found in many European cities, old villas and buildings with projecting balconies

facts.rationale: Fontainhas is Panaji's old Latin quarter with Portuguese-influenced architecture and narrow streets. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is an old Latin quarter in Panjim, capital city of the state of Goa, India. It maintains its Portuguese influence
on a planned grid system after the Portuguese relocated the capital from Old Goa

facts.rationale: Portuguese colonial capital with colonial houses; Fontainhas keeps Portuguese influence. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district
Panaji, town, capital of Goa state, western India. It lies on the estuary of the Mandavi River at the river’s mouth on the Arabian Sea.

facts.rationale: Capital of Goa. (A and B agree on all fields.) Adjudicator checked Wikipedia/other quotes verbatim; UNESCO/Britannica pages return 403 to the adjudicator, quotes kept as given by both labellers.

sources.quote: Panaji, the state capital, and Old Goa, the former capital of Goa, are both situated on the left bank of the Mandovi.
Set on the southern left bank of the Mandovi River skirting the town

facts.rationale: Left bank of the west-flowing Mandovi = south bank; at the estuary mouth on the Arabian Sea. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is a hill neighbourhood of Panaji, the state capital of India's smallest state Goa
lies at the spot where the Mandovi and the Zuari rivers meet and flow into the Arabian Sea

facts.rationale: Altinho is a hill neighbourhood; Dona Paula is the headland where the Mandovi and Zuari meet, a few km south-west of the centre (Wikipedia counts it within Panaji city). (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district
Panaji, the state capital, and Old Goa, the former capital of Goa, are both situated on the left bank of the Mandovi.

facts.rationale: Capital of Goa on the south (left) bank of the Mandovi. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: also known as Panjim, is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district
also known as Panjim

facts.rationale: Panaji official, also known as Panjim; restates name/alias. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is a hill neighbourhood of Panaji, the state capital of India's smallest state Goa
considered an elite residential colony, with the State's chief minister's residence and the Archbishop's palace located here

facts.rationale: Hill residential neighbourhood with the Archbishop's palace; 'colonial-era bungalows' not explicitly sourced but core claim holds. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district
Set on the southern left bank of the Mandovi River skirting the town

facts.rationale: State capital at the Mandovi mouth on the Arabian Sea. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: narrow and picturesque winding streets like those found in many European cities, old villas and buildings with projecting balconies
painted in the traditional tones of pale yellow, green, or blue, and roofs made of red coloured tiles

facts.rationale: Fontainhas (with Sao Tome, listed together by Goa Tourism) has Portuguese-style narrow lanes and coloured houses. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of the North Goa district

facts.rationale: Capital of Goa. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim
In 1843, the capital was moved to Panjim (Nova Goa or New Goa)

facts.rationale: Capital shifted from Old Goa to Panjim in 1843. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim
It was previously the territorial capital of the former Portuguese India (Estado da Índia).

facts.rationale: In 1843 Panjim replaced Old Goa as capital of the Estado da India. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: In the late eighteenth century, a Goan expatriate named António João de Sequeira (nicknamed Mossmikar)
painted in the traditional tones of pale yellow, green, or blue, and roofs made of red coloured tiles

facts.rationale: Heritage quarter founded late 18th century with painted Portuguese-style houses; exact colour list (ochre/terracotta) differs slightly from sources (pale yellow, green, blue). (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: Panaji, the state capital, and Old Goa, the former capital of Goa, are both situated on the left bank of the Mandovi.
Set on the southern left bank of the Mandovi River skirting the town

facts.rationale: South (left) bank near the Mandovi mouth. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: In 1843, the capital was moved to Panjim (Nova Goa or New Goa)
after a devastating epidemic decimated the population of the Cidade de Goa (Old Goa) in the mid-18th century.

facts.rationale: Britannica: plagues forced abandonment of Old Goa; Panaji capital in 1843. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: Dona Paula (Named after Dona Paula de Souto Maior) is a neighborhood and tourist destination in the city of Panaji, Goa, India.
lies at the spot where the Mandovi and the Zuari rivers meet and flow into the Arabian Sea

facts.rationale: Dona Paula is a neighbourhood of Panaji at the Mandovi–Zuari confluence before the Arabian Sea. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim
In 1843, the capital was moved to Panjim (Nova Goa or New Goa)

facts.rationale: Capital moved in 1843, not 1706. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: Panaji, the state capital, and Old Goa, the former capital of Goa, are both situated on the left bank of the Mandovi.
Set on the southern left bank of the Mandovi River skirting the town

facts.rationale: South bank, near the estuary on the Arabian Sea. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: Panaji, the state capital, and Old Goa, the former capital of Goa, are both situated on the left bank of the Mandovi.
A new Legislative Assembly complex was inaugurated in March 2000, across the Mandovi River

facts.rationale: Panaji is on the left (south) bank; Porvorim lies across the river on the north side. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: signed the Instrument of Surrender on 19 December 1961, thus ending 450 years of Portuguese rule in India
It became a state-capital on Goa's elevation to statehood in 1987 and between 1961 and 1987 it was the capital of the Union Territory

facts.rationale: About 450 years of Portuguese rule ended 1961; UT capital 1961-87, state capital from 1987. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim
It was previously the territorial capital of the former Portuguese India (Estado da Índia).

facts.rationale: Capital of Portuguese India from 1843 until the 1961 annexation. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: signed the Instrument of Surrender on 19 December 1961, thus ending 450 years of Portuguese rule in India
Panaji was annexed by India with the rest of Goa and the former Portuguese territories after the Indian annexation of Portuguese India in 1961.

facts.rationale: Portuguese rule ended in 1961. (A and B agree on all fields.)

sources.quote: It continued to be the de jure capital of Goa until 1843, when the capital was shifted to Panjim
In 1843, the capital was moved to Panjim (Nova Goa or New Goa)

facts.rationale: Capital from 1843, replacing Old Goa. (A and B agree on all fields.)

is a hill neighbourhood of Panaji, the state capital of India's smallest state Goa.

facts.rationale: Altinho is a hill neighbourhood of Panaji. (A and B agree on all fields.)

is an old Latin quarter in Panjim, capital city of the state of Goa, India. It maintains its Portuguese influence
